boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on Park Street, Broad Street, Fourth Avenue, Main Street, and Third Avenue just beyond Grinnell College.

cards.title: Central Park Gazebo
cards.subtitle: Third Avenue corridor, downtown Grinnell
cards.notes: Walk the Third Avenue edge of Central Park to see the gazebo, accessible playground, restrooms, and water features listed by the city.
cards.short_summary: A civic-park stop with a gazebo and public amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Central Park Gazebo at 925 Third Avenue and identifies a gazebo, playground, accessible restrooms, and water among its features.
cards.access_notes: City parks are closed daily from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.; the gazebo may be rented.

cards.title: Grinnell Veterans Monument
cards.subtitle: Central Park along the Fourth Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Approach through Central Park to view the 42-foot steel work and follow its spiral path into the open-air center for quiet reflection.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in public monument shaped like an unfurling flag.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the Grinnell Veterans Monument as a 42-foot steel sculpture in Central Park, with a spiral path leading to an open-air center.
cards.access_notes: Located in Central Park; observe the city's park closure hours.

cards.title: Grinnell City Hall
cards.subtitle: Fourth Avenue corridor, downtown Grinnell
cards.notes: Step into the City Hall lobby on Fourth Avenue to look for the historical Spaulding buggies and car chassis displayed in the connected building.
cards.short_summary: City offices paired with a small transportation-history display.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell Historical Museum states that visitors can view Spaulding buggies and a Spaulding car chassis at Grinnell City Hall, 520 Fourth Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Museum-listed display hours are Tuesday–Friday 1–5 p.m. and Saturday noon–4 p.m.

cards.title: Grinnell Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Broad Street corridor, downtown Grinnell
cards.notes: Use Broad Street to reach the Arts Center and check its current calendar for gallery, theatre, or arts-education programming before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A downtown arts building with gallery, theatre, and education space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell Area Arts Council lists the Grinnell Arts Center at 926 Broad Street with arts education space, Loft Theatre, and Stewart Gallery.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; Saturday during exhibits 10 a.m.–noon; closed Monday.

cards.title: The Stew Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Broad Street corridor, beside the Arts Center
cards.notes: Find this Broad Street workspace next to the Arts Center, then consult its calendar for access to making tools and scheduled activities.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown workspace for hands-on arts and fabrication.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell Area Arts Council lists The Stew Makerspace at 927 Broad Street with wood, craft, visual-arts, 3D-printing, laser-cutting, pottery, metal, and textile equipment.
cards.access_notes: The Arts Council directs visitors to its calendar for makerspace hours and access details.

cards.title: Drake Community Library
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor, downtown Grinnell
cards.notes: Walk Park Street to the public library for a reading break, then use its current events calendar or browse its local-history resources.
cards.short_summary: The city’s public library and a documented local-history steward.
cards.evidence_claim: Drake Community Library lists its location as 930 Park Street and publishes current hours and an events calendar.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Sunday 2–5 p.m.; Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Friday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Hotel Grinnell
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor, across from Central Park
cards.notes: Use Park Street to see the exterior and photo gallery of the repurposed 1921 junior-high building; reserve rooms or events only if needed.
cards.short_summary: A former school building adapted as a downtown hotel.
cards.evidence_claim: Hotel Grinnell identifies its address as 925 Park Street and describes the building as a repurposed 1921 Grinnell junior high school.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing does not require a reservation; lodging and event access are subject to the hotel's arrangements.

cards.title: Beckman Gallery & Gifts
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, downtown Grinnell
cards.notes: Follow Main Street to this custom-framing and gift shop, and use the store’s posted hours to plan a daytime stop for framing or browsing.
cards.short_summary: A locally operated framing and gift destination on Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Beckman Gallery & Gifts identifies itself as a custom-framing and gift shop at 912 Main Street in downtown Grinnell.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: Bates Flowers by Design
cards.subtitle: Fourth Avenue corridor, downtown Grinnell
cards.notes: Stop along Fourth Avenue to browse floral designs, plants, cards, and chocolates; confirm availability or delivery details directly before purchasing.
cards.short_summary: A Fourth Avenue florist with gifts and plant options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell Area Chamber lists Bates Flowers by Design at 813 Fourth Avenue and describes its flowers, plants, chocolates, greeting cards, and gifts.
cards.source_title: Bates Flowers by Design — Grinnell Area Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: The Chamber lists daytime Monday–Saturday hours and advises confirming hours with the business.

cards.title: McMurray House
cards.subtitle: Broad Street corridor, north of campus
cards.notes: Walk Broad Street for an exterior look at the 1895 Victorian McMurray House; contact museum staff well ahead if you want to ask about a tour.
cards.short_summary: A documented Victorian house associated with Grinnell’s historical museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell Historical Museum identifies McMurray House at 1125 Broad Street as a 1895 Victorian house with original woodwork, decorative windows, and fixtures.
cards.access_notes: The museum currently marks the house closed to the public; tour inquiries require at least three business days’ notice.
